I’ve been feeling so down since my husband passed away about a year and a half ago—almost every day since. I cry often, sometimes over little things, and I can’t seem to pull myself together. I sleep a lot, too—just stay in bed for hours during the day, even if I slept through the night. It’s like I don’t have the energy to get up or do anything. Even deciding what to wear or what to eat feels overwhelming. I’ve stood in the kitchen staring at the fridge, paralyzed, like I can’t trust myself to choose.

There were times—especially in the first few months—I thought I couldn’t go on without him. I even thought about how, if I took too many of my pain pills at night, no one might find me until the next day. But those thoughts never turned into real plans—I knew I couldn’t do that to my kids.

The sadness really started after he died—within weeks, honestly—and even though some days are better, I still don’t feel like myself. I know this loss is hard, but I didn’t expect it would still be this heavy after all this time.
